issue_text:
Please pull up my round-trip airline reservation C4C633 and give me the complete details: the full itinerary, both passengers, how many bags are already attached, whether insurance is on it, and the payment history. The outbound on C4C633 is the SEA to SAN segment, the return flight on that booking is FL84B16B on 2026-10-05, and C4C633 currently has standard insurance on it.

While you’re in that reservation, also check the current status of outbound flight FLE7F420 on 2026-10-01 and tell me whether that segment still looks normal.
summary: A long multi-domain session anchored on flight booking C4C633. T1 pulled the full round-trip record (outbound FLE7F420 SEA→SAN Oct 1; return FL84B16B SAN→SEA Oct 5; standard insurance) — the source of all three traps. T2–T4 are capability refusals: the user asks to rename a passenger, 'process' a flight change, and add a bag, and each time the agent correctly recognises there is no write tool and reports no change made. T5 looked up a second booking EC4C1C, T6 sent a verified text to Jordan Kim, and T7 ran a shopping block (product search, return policy, process a return for Jordan Lee, pull the profile). The contradictions all spring in T8, where the user asks the agent to confirm three false C4C633 claims (return = FLE7F420; outbound = SAN→SEA; no insurance); the agent checked each against the record and marked all three 'incorrect', restating the true values — DETECT+REJECT ×3 (6/9 subgoals credited; recall/detect pass, flags fail). T9 wraps up and re-states that the three false claims were correctly identified. The agent was consistently accurate about both tool limits and stored facts, but never converted a detection into a clarifying question.
